prompt: I need extra thinking time and would rather practise in writing. Help me prepare an interview accommodation request; I do not want to disclose my diagnosis. The jurisdiction is unknown.
response:
We can practise entirely in writing, one question at a time, with as much thinking time as you need. You do not need to tell me your diagnosis.

Here is a request you can adapt:

Subject: Interview adjustment request — [role / interview date]

Hello [name],

Thank you for inviting me to interview. I would like to request some adjustments so I can demonstrate my experience effectively: written questions alongside any spoken questions, and additional thinking time before answering. It would also help to receive the interview format and agenda in advance.

I prefer to keep medical details private and focus on the practical adjustments I need. Could you let me know how to arrange these and who handles requests confidentially? If you require supporting information, please explain what is needed and how it will be used.

Thank you,
[name]

Your preference for written practice does not have to become a request for a wholly written interview. If that would also help you in the actual interview, add: “Would a written response format be possible for some or all questions?”

Because the jurisdiction and employer process are unknown, this is a practical request rather than a statement of legal entitlement. Documentation requirements can vary; I cannot promise that no medical information will be requested. Start with the adjustments and ask what minimum information their process requires before sharing anything further.
